jp: 明日[あした]、先生[せんせい]に{会[あ]い|nt-homophone}に行[い]きます。
en: Tomorrow I am going to go and see my teacher.
why: Going to see a person is 会う, with 会 (to meet, gather).

jp: 久[ひさ]しぶりに友達[ともだち]と{会[あ]う|nt-homophone}予定[よてい]です。
en: I plan to meet a friend for the first time in a long while.
why: Meeting someone is 会う; 合う means to match or fit.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]に祖母[そぼ]に{会[あ]って|nt-homophone}、一緒[いっしょ]に昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べました。
en: On the weekend I saw my grandmother and we had lunch together.
why: Seeing a person is 会う, written with 会.

jp: この靴[くつ]は私[わたし]の足[あし]にぴったり{合[あ]い|nt-homophone}ます。
en: These shoes fit my feet perfectly.
why: Fitting or matching is 合う, written with 合 (to join, fit).

jp: あの二人[ふたり]は趣味[しゅみ]が{合[あ]う|nt-homophone}ので、よく話[はな]しています。
en: Those two share the same interests, so they often talk.
why: Tastes that match are 合う, not the 会 of meeting people.

jp: 答[こた]えが{合[あ]って|nt-homophone}いるか、先生[せんせい]に見[み]てもらいました。
en: I had the teacher check whether my answers were correct.
why: Answers that are correct match the key: 合う.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、帰[かえ]り道[みち]で急[きゅう]に雨[あめ]に{遭[あ]い|nt-homophone}ました。
en: Yesterday on the way home I was suddenly caught in the rain.
why: Running into something unpleasant (rain, an accident) is 遭う.

jp: 駅前[えきまえ]の喫茶店[きっさてん]で十時[じゅうじ]に{会[あ]い|nt-homophone}ましょう。
en: Let's meet at the coffee shop in front of the station at ten.
why: Arranging to meet a person is 会う.

jp: このスープは私[わたし]の口[くち]に{合[あ]い|nt-homophone}ません。
en: This soup does not suit my taste.
why: Food that suits your palate is 口に合う, written with 合.

jp: 空港[くうこう]で三年[さんねん]ぶりに姉[あね]に{会[あ]った|nt-homophone}とき、とてもうれしかったです。
en: I was very happy when I met my older sister at the airport after three years.
why: Seeing a person you know is 会う.

jp: 時計[とけい]を{合[あ]わ|nt-homophone}せましょう。みんなの時間[じかん]が同[おな]じになります。
en: Let's synchronise our watches so that everyone has the same time.
why: Setting a watch to match another is 時計を合わせる, with 合.

jp: 今日[きょう]は朝[あさ]から{暑[あつ]い|nt-homophone}ですね。
en: It has been hot since this morning, hasn't it?
why: Hot weather or air is 暑い; 熱い is for things you touch or drink.

jp: {熱[あつ]い|nt-homophone}お茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]んで、体[からだ]が温[あたた]まりました。
en: I drank hot tea and my body warmed up.
why: Hot tea, a hot object or a fever is 熱い, with 熱 (heat).

jp: このパンは{厚[あつ]い|nt-homophone}ので、半分[はんぶん]に切[き]って食[た]べます。
en: This bread is thick, so I will cut it in half and eat it.
why: Thickness of a flat object is 厚い, with 厚 (thick).

jp: 夏[なつ]の{暑[あつ]い|nt-homophone}日[ひ]は、冷[つめ]たい麦茶[むぎちゃ]がおいしいです。
en: On hot summer days, cold barley tea tastes good.
why: A hot day describes the weather, so 暑い.

jp: お風呂[ふろ]のお湯[ゆ]が{熱[あつ]|nt-homophone}すぎて、入[はい]れません。
en: The bath water is too hot and I cannot get in.
why: Hot water you touch is 熱い, not the 暑 of air temperature.

jp: 寒[さむ]いので、{厚[あつ]い|nt-homophone}コートを着[き]て出[で]かけました。
en: It was cold, so I went out wearing a thick coat.
why: A coat with bulk is thick: 厚い.

jp: この辞書[じしょ]はとても{厚[あつ]い|nt-homophone}ですが、軽[かる]いです。
en: This dictionary is very thick, but it is light.
why: Thickness of a book is 厚い.

jp: フライパンが{熱[あつ]く|nt-homophone}なっているので、気[き]をつけてください。
en: The frying pan has become hot, so please be careful.
why: A hot pan you could burn yourself on is 熱い.

jp: エアコンをつけても、部屋[へや]が{暑[あつ]く|nt-homophone}て眠[ねむ]れません。
en: Even with the air conditioner on, the room is hot and I cannot sleep.
why: The hot air of a room is 暑い.

jp: 今年[ことし]の夏[なつ]は去年[きょねん]より{暑[あつ]い|nt-homophone}でしょう。
en: This summer will probably be hotter than last year.
why: Summer weather is 暑い.

jp: 冬[ふゆ]は{厚[あつ]い|nt-homophone}靴下[くつした]をはいて寝[ね]ます。
en: In winter I sleep wearing thick socks.
why: Thick socks are 厚い.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]をひいたので、{熱[あつ]い|nt-homophone}おかゆを食[た]べました。
en: I had a cold, so I ate hot rice porridge.
why: Hot food you eat or touch is 熱い, with 熱 (heat), not the 暑 of weather.

jp: 明日[あした]は朝[あさ]が{早[はや]い|nt-homophone}ので、もう寝[ね]ます。
en: Tomorrow morning is early, so I am going to bed now.
why: Early in time is 早い, with 早 (early).

jp: 新幹線[しんかんせん]は、バスよりずっと{速[はや]い|nt-homophone}です。
en: The Shinkansen is much faster than a bus.
why: High speed of a vehicle is 速い, with 速 (speed).

jp: {早[はや]く|nt-homophone}起[お]きて、公園[こうえん]を散歩[さんぽ]しました。
en: I got up early and took a walk in the park.
why: Getting up at an early hour is 早く, about time rather than speed.

jp: この川[かわ]は流[なが]れが{速[はや]い|nt-homophone}ので、泳[およ]いではいけません。
en: This river has a fast current, so you must not swim in it.
why: The speed of a current is 速い.

jp: 母[はは]は毎朝[まいあさ]、私[わたし]より{早[はや]く|nt-homophone}起[お]きます。
en: My mother gets up earlier than I do every morning.
why: Earlier in the day is 早く.

jp: 野球[やきゅう]の投手[とうしゅ]は、{速[はや]い|nt-homophone}球[たま]を投[な]げます。
en: The baseball pitcher throws fast balls.
why: A ball with high speed is 速い.

jp: この車[くるま]は時速[じそく]二百[にひゃく]キロで走[はし]る、{速[はや]い|nt-homophone}車[くるま]です。
en: This car is a fast car that runs at two hundred kilometres an hour.
why: Speed in km per hour is 速い, with 速.

jp: 夏[なつ]は夜明[よあ]けが{早[はや]い|nt-homophone}ので、朝[あさ]から明[あか]るいです。
en: In summer dawn comes early, so it is light from early morning.
why: Dawn arriving early in time is 早い.

jp: 風[かぜ]が強[つよ]くて、雲[くも]の動[うご]きが{速[はや]い|nt-homophone}です。
en: The wind is strong and the clouds are moving fast.
why: Clouds moving at speed is 速い, a matter of speed, not time.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]、寝[ね]る前[まえ]にラジオを{聞[き]き/聴[き]き|nt-homophone}ます。
en: Every night I listen to the radio before going to bed.
why: Listening to sound is 聞く (or 聴く), with an ear inside; 効く means to take effect.

jp: この目薬[めぐすり]はよく{効[き]き|nt-homophone}ますよ。
en: These eye drops work very well.
why: A medicine that works is 効く, with 効 (effect).

jp: 友達[ともだち]から、来月[らいげつ]引[ひ]っ越[こ]すと{聞[き]い|nt-homophone}ました。
en: I heard from a friend that they are moving next month.
why: Hearing news is 聞く.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]を引[ひ]いたときは、この薬[くすり]が{効[き]く|nt-homophone}と思[おも]います。
en: I think this medicine works when you have a cold.
why: Medicine acting on an illness is 効く.

jp: 夜[よる]、外[そと]で猫[ねこ]の鳴[な]き声[ごえ]を{聞[き]き|nt-homophone}ました。
en: At night I heard a cat meowing outside.
why: Sounds you hear are 聞く.

jp: 痛[いた]み止[ど]めを飲[の]んだら、すぐに{効[き]い|nt-homophone}てきました。
en: After I took a painkiller, it started to work right away.
why: A painkiller taking effect is 効く.

jp: 電話[でんわ]でニュースを{聞[き]い|nt-homophone}て、すぐに会社[かいしゃ]へ向[む]かいました。
en: I heard the news over the phone and headed straight to the office.
why: Hearing news is 聞く, not the 効 of effect.

jp: 遠[とお]くで雷[かみなり]の音[おと]が{聞[き]こえ|nt-homophone}ました。
en: I could hear the sound of thunder in the distance.
why: Sound that reaches the ear is 聞こえる, written with 聞.

jp: 寒[さむ]いので、厚[あつ]いコートを{着[き]る|nt-homophone}ことにしました。
en: It was cold, so I decided to wear a thick coat.
why: Putting clothes on the body is 着る, with 着.

jp: 誕生日[たんじょうび]に、母[はは]はケーキを八[やっ]つに{切[き]り|nt-homophone}ました。
en: On my birthday my mother cut the cake into eight pieces.
why: Cutting a cake into pieces is 切る, with the 切 of knife and cut.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]、制服[せいふく]を{着[き]て|nt-homophone}学校[がっこう]へ行[い]きます。
en: Every morning I put on my uniform and go to school.
why: A uniform is worn: 着る.

jp: 髪[かみ]が長[なが]くなったので、美容院[びよういん]で{切[き]って|nt-homophone}もらいました。
en: My hair had grown long, so I had it cut at the hairdresser's.
why: Cutting hair is 切る.

jp: {切[き]った|nt-homophone}野菜[やさい]を鍋[なべ]に入[い]れてください。
en: Please put the cut vegetables into the pot.
why: Vegetables are cut with a knife: 切る.

jp: 今日[きょう]は着物[きもの]を{着[き]て|nt-homophone}、お祭[まつ]りに行[い]きます。
en: Today I am going to the festival wearing a kimono.
why: Wearing a kimono is 着る.

jp: 電話[でんわ]を{切[き]る|nt-homophone}前[まえ]に、もう一度[いちど]お礼[れい]を言[い]いました。
en: Before hanging up the phone, I thanked them once more.
why: Ending a call is 電話を切る, with 切.

jp: 浴衣[ゆかた]は、夏[なつ]に{着[き]る|nt-homophone}服[ふく]です。
en: A yukata is clothing that you wear in summer.
why: Clothing is worn: 着る.

jp: はさみで紙[かみ]を{切[き]り|nt-homophone}ましょう。
en: Let's cut the paper with scissors.
why: Cutting paper with scissors is 切る.

jp: 明日[あした]は早[はや]く家[いえ]に{帰[かえ]る|nt-homophone}つもりです。
en: Tomorrow I intend to go home early.
why: Going back home is 帰る; 変える means to change something.

jp: 父[ちち]は髪型[かみがた]を{変[か]える|nt-homophone}ことにしました。
en: My father decided to change his hairstyle.
why: Changing a state or look is 変える, with 変 (change).

jp: 家[いえ]に{帰[かえ]る|nt-homophone}前[まえ]に、スーパーで買[か]い物[もの]をします。
en: Before going home, I do some shopping at the supermarket.
why: Returning to one's home is 帰る.

jp: 古[ふる]い計画[けいかく]を{変[か]える|nt-homophone}必要[ひつよう]があります。
en: We need to change the old plan.
why: Altering a plan is 変える.

jp: 疲[つか]れたので、今日[きょう]は先[さき]に{帰[かえ]る|nt-homophone}と言[い]っています。
en: They are tired, so they say they will go home first today.
why: Leaving for home is 帰る.

jp: 色[いろ]を{変[か]える|nt-homophone}と、部屋[へや]の感[かん]じが明[あか]るくなります。
en: If you change the colour, the feel of the room becomes brighter.
why: Making a colour different is 変える.

jp: 国[くに]へ{帰[かえ]る|nt-homophone}友達[ともだち]を、空港[くうこう]まで送[おく]りました。
en: I saw off a friend who is returning to their country as far as the airport.
why: Returning to one's own country is 帰る.

jp: 考[かんが]えを{変[か]える|nt-homophone}のは、簡単[かんたん]ではありません。
en: Changing one's mind is not easy.
why: Changing one's mind is 変える.

jp: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りそうだから、早[はや]く{帰[かえ]る|nt-homophone}ほうがいいですよ。
en: It looks like rain, so you had better go home early.
why: Heading home is 帰る.
